articles.title: Framework Benchmarks: Compare Frontend Frameworks
articles.description: An experienced developer built and benchmarked the same app across numerous frameworks (e.g. Angular, Solid, React, Alpine.js…). Here are the results, covering bundle size, build time, UX metrics, and more.
articles.author: Alicia Sykes

articles.title: Nuxt 4.5 Released: The Full-Stack Vue Framework
articles.description: Daniel Roe calls it the biggest release in a while: Vite 8, Rspack 2, experimental SSR streaming, a new useLayout composable, and a lot of preparation for Nuxt 5. Nuxt 3 users take note: it goes end of life July 31.
articles.author: Nuxt Team

articles.title: How a Fake Interview's Coding Challenge Steals Credentials
articles.description: A dissection of a North Korean campaign that hides malware inside SVG images in a fake job interview's JavaScript 'coding challenge'. The targeting of job-seeking devs is on the increase, as Roman Imankulov recently discovered first-hand.
articles.author: Daniel Stepanic (Elastic)

articles.title: Handling Concurrency on the Web with Web Locks API
articles.description: The Web Locks API is a widely available browser API to allow tabs or workers with the same origin to hold and release locks.
articles.author: Cesar Contreras

articles.title: Engineering High-Performance Parsers with Data-Oriented Design
articles.description: A look into how data-oriented design helped build Yuku, a JavaScript parser that's faster than alternatives like Oxc, SWC or Babel (you can give it a spin here).
articles.author: Arshad Yaseen

articles.title: Flint: Chart Specs that Compile to Vega-Lite, ECharts, or Chart.js
articles.description: A Microsoft project that compiles a simple, declarative JSON-based spec of a data visualization into a form that Vega-Lite, ECharts or Chart.js can render. It's pitched at agentic use, but is a simple intermediate format humans could benefit from too.
articles.author: Microsoft Research

articles.title: unwasm: Import .wasm Files Like Any Other ES Module
articles.description: Build-time tooling for when WASM is part of a bundled app and you want it to feel more like a normal module (e.g. import { sum } from "sum.wasm").
articles.author: unjs

articles.title: BotKit: Build Standalone ActivityPub Bots
articles.description: A way to run a bot (or multiple bots) that Mastodon users can see and follow but without needing an account anywhere. Write it all in JavaScript and self-host with Deno, Node.js or even Cloudflare Workers.
articles.author: Fedify

articles.title: 🎨 Color.js 0.7: 'Let’s Get Serious About Color'
articles.description: A fantastic library for working with colors, following the latest specs. v0.7 is a big update with support for new color spaces, a new gamut mapping method, and a smarter display() fallback for colors not natively supported by a browser.
articles.author: Lea Verou and Chris Lilley

articles.description: Vue 3.6 is now in Release Candidate stage – Vapor Mode, first teased over two years ago, is now feature complete and ready to go.
Angular is switching to a yearly release cadence, with v23 scheduled for June 2027, a year after v22 dropped.
ESLint now offers official 'codemods' for automating ESLint version migrations, with v8→v9 and v9→v10 available.
🇫🇷 An official Three.js conference is coming to Paris, France, this September 10-11. Three.js developer Mr.doob will, of course, be there.
Preact 11.0 Beta 2 – "One of the last betas for Preact 11," says maintainer Jovi De Croock. There's already a migration guide ready to use.
WebStorm 2026.2 – JetBrains' JavaScript IDE adds TypeScript 7 support, and enhances support for Svelte and Vue.
Astro 7.1, Rslint 0.7, Rolldown 1.2, actions/setup-node@v7

articles.title: ⚽️ Rebuilding FIFA's Standings Layout with CSS Subgrid
articles.description: The World Cup is over now, but this is an interesting design problem worth unpicking and understanding. Ahmad approaches it with CSS grid, subgrid, and more, showing how to achieve a responsive, complex layout. Clean result, no messi. Excellent visual explainer, with code examples aplenty.
articles.author: Ahmad Shadeed

articles.title: 📱 Low and Mid-Tier Mobile for the Real World
articles.description: An update to a guide on picking representative test devices in 2026 (while reminding us that the newest phone isn't always the right one). This year's picks include the Galaxy A17 5G (5th best-seller globally in Q1) and Galaxy A56 5G (Europe's 2025 #1).
articles.author: Harry Roberts

articles.title: How Figma Built Accessibility Into a Canvas-Based Product
articles.description: Canvas-rendered UIs get none of the browser's accessibility features for free, so Figma had to recreate screen reader support, keyboard navigation, and focus management from scratch.
articles.author: David Winslow & Elynn Lee (Figma)

articles.title: Time-Based Background Colour Transitions with Temporal and CSS color-mix
articles.description: A nice example of using the Temporal API to grab a user's local time via PlainTime. This is then used to change a site's theme depending on the time of day. Neat!
articles.author: Sophie Koonin

articles.title: Return of CSS Outline
articles.description: Makes the case for keeping focus outlines, a small but important accessibility detail. Plenty of sites still ship with outline: 0, found in old CSS resets, often leaving keyboard users unable to see what's focused — despite :focus-visible making this a solved problem.
articles.author: Morgan Murrah

articles.title: 🤖 Which AI Actually Reads Your Site? Two Months of LLM Traffic, Measured
articles.description: You can make your site readable by LLMs, but do such 'AI SEO' efforts work? After tracking server logs for two months, here's a look at how it can shake out.
articles.author: Rita Klubochkina

articles.title: Under My Radar: The Highlight API, text-indent and font-family: math
articles.description: Spotlights three CSS features that are now Baseline: the Custom Highlight API for DOM-free text highlighting, text-indent for print-style typography, and font-family: math for accessible formula rendering. Code and demos included for all three.
articles.author: Brecht De Ruyte

articles.title: Masonry (with Animation) in CSS
articles.description: Chris explores fluid animation in masonry-style layouts using CSS Grid and Anchor Positioning, with a nod to the newly-arriving grid-lanes.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: Animating the <details> Element with Only CSS
articles.description: A clean way to animate this HTML element, toggling the open/close with pure CSS.
articles.author: Austin Gil

articles.title: Jelly UI: Soft Web Components
articles.description: A dependency-free web components library that brings 'soft' physics effects to native HTML controls. There's 40 elements included, and you can get a feel for them via the showcase.
articles.author: bmson

articles.title: Introducing Babylon Lite: A Smaller, WebGPU-Only 3D Engine
articles.description: BabylonJS is a powerful, long-standing 3D engine for the web. But the Babylon team have had a go at creating something new from scratch. The result is Lite — a much faster and smaller engine (with some tradeoffs).
articles.author: Babylon.js Team

articles.title: 📊 Framework Benchmarks: Compare Frontend Frameworks
articles.description: An experienced dev built the same weather app in numerous frameworks (Angular, React, etc…) along with an automated benchmarking system for them. Here's the results, covering bundle size, build time, UX metrics, and more.
articles.author: Alicia Sykes

articles.title: edge-aura: Give Your Viewport an Organic Screen-Edge Glow
articles.description: A Canvas 2D effect for adding a full-viewport organic glow at the screen edge with no CSS required.
articles.author: Takuya Jodai

articles.title: A11Y.md: A Context System for Building Accessible Software by Default
articles.description: Integrates with your AI agents (Cursor, Claude, etc.), based on 'enforceable rules' aligned with WCAG guidelines.
articles.author: Felipe Arriaga Carriço

articles.title: Decoy Font: A TTF Font That Hides What You Type
articles.description: A free font designed to hide what you're typing from AI by misleading it with a 'decoy'. The font uses "separate spatial frequencies to communicate two different letters in the same space". I found slightly blurring my vision made this easier to see. An interesting experiment!
articles.author: Mixfont
